sampling_model.design: \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,Z_i,X_i)\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), with fixed \(K\) and a fixed number of cross-fitting folds.
sampling_model.units: Independent study participants with bounded continuous outcomes and pretreatment covariates.
sampling_model.treatment: \(J_i\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\) is latent and ordered; \(A_i\) and \(Z_i\) are paired categorical measurements.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each training fold fits one label-aligned product law without using unknown measurement supports, the true conditional Gram matrix, or its rank. All posterior and projection objects are plug-in implications; the Gram inverse uses the fitted spectrum above \(\varepsilon/2\), and fitted low-mass measurement cells yield estimable support-leakage diagnostics.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: As the discretization becomes sufficiently fine, the approach recovers the efficiency bound asymptotically.
A valid influence function is obtained for categorical hidden actions using inverse-feature product bridges.
The parameters of the model are uniquely identifiable, up to label swapping.
The estimators are efficient if computed under the truth.
We present a constructive identification argument and use it to develop simple two-step estimators of the component distributions and all their functionals.
Semiparametric theory for array-decomposition causal effects remains relatively nascent.
The joint law of observables and the continuously distributed latent variable is identified under three-measurement operator conditions and a labeling restriction.
Triple proxies identify causal functionals by applying continuous full-law recovery, up to an invertible transformation when labels are not normalized.

body.tldr: For every fixed \(K\geq3\), every observed-data DQM score has a measurable conditional-\(X\), uniformly bounded, support-preserving lift to centered additive latent-factor scores. Hence the full observed tangent closure is the latent score-image closure, and the exact continuous-outcome canonical gradient is obtained by a pointwise \(K^2\)-cell projection followed by one conditional Gram solve. The implementable score uses one non-oracle fitted product law, a computable spectral cutoff \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), and explicit support-leakage allowances; efficient cross-fitted Gaussian and maximum-\(t\) inference requires the stated operator, screening, leakage, and product-rate conditions.

project_justification.gap: The binary hidden-treatment literature characterizes efficiency but computes the continuous-outcome correction through the specific partition-dependent sequence in Supplement S8.2, while the categorical product-bridge literature establishes validity without observed-data canonicality. Existing continuous three-proxy full-law identification does not supply the uniformly bounded derivative inverse needed for tangent completeness.
project_justification.niche: Fixed latent cardinality, quantitative three-view separation, and paired categorical measurements make it possible to eliminate the infinite outcome nuisance pointwise and expose a finite conditional information operator.
project_justification.fill: The project differentiates the separated three-view factorization and proves a measurable uniformly bounded right inverse from every observed DQM score to factorwise centered latent additive scores, including support-preserving recovery of the class-density score. This closes tangent-space completeness and validates the finite projector as the canonical correction. The attaining estimator is non-oracle: a fixed \(\varepsilon/2\) spectral cutoff selects the fitted Gram directions on the separated event, while estimable low-mass diagnostics expose structural-zero leakage in the remainder and inference conditions.

body.related_work: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) are the closest theorem-level comparator: their Theorems 2--4 treat the binary observed tangent space and influence functions, and Supplement S8.2 obtains the continuous-outcome efficiency bound through a refining outcome partition. The present multilevel construction instead proves a conditional differential score lift and uses the exact \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^+B^{\mathsf T}\) followed by one conditional Gram solve. Bian, Zhou, and Cui (2026) supply the categorical inverse-feature product-bridge precursor, but not observed-data canonicality or the non-oracle projected-score remainder. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009), Hu and Schennach (2008), and Deaner (2023) inform latent-factor identification; their level-identification results do not furnish the measurable uniformly bounded DQM right inverse proved here. Tsiatis and Ma (2004) inform nuisance-score projection, Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2016) inform coherent repeated-measurement estimation, and Tsybakov (2009) informs the smooth sieve benchmark. The implementation result does not assume access to a true measurement support or a true Gram rank; design-known supports are an optional specialization.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The non-oracle Gram correction is certified on the event \(\|\widehat G-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\varepsilon/4\): thresholding at \(\varepsilon/2\) selects exactly the true number of nonzero directions, and the thresholded inverse differs from \(G^+\) by at most \(14\varepsilon^{-2}\|\widehat G-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\); an unconditional conditional-\(L^2\) bound holds with constant \(26\varepsilon^{-2}\). For unknown measurement supports, \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\) makes the low-mass screen cover all true structural-zero cells with high probability, but the resulting \(\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n}\) contribution is first order. Thus a generic coordinatewise smooth rate for the primitive factors does not by itself prove root-\(n\) inference when structural zeros are present.
body.honest_scope: The exact identification, tangent-space, finite-projector, canonical-gradient, strict-variance, binary-comparison, and continuous-witness claims remain restricted to the declared fixed-\(K\), separated, pathwise-interior model. The cross-fitted implementation uses no unknown measurement support and no oracle Gram rank. Its fitted Gram inverse is selected spectrally at \(\varepsilon/2\); score stability additionally tracks uniform Gram error. With unknown supports, inference requires both \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\) and the corrected \(\Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})\), whose additive leakage terms need not be quadratic. If the study protocol supplies support sets, enforcing those observed zeros sets the corresponding leakage allowances to zero. The smooth B-spline question must therefore establish primitive and derived operator rates, uniform support-screening rates, and sufficiently fast leakage; the old coordinatewise \(\rho_n\) assertion alone is not enough. Modal ties, local singularity, and support patterns that cannot be screened at the required rate remain outside efficient-inference delivery. The maternal-smoking application remains prospective because the published six-bin study does not itself verify paired-proxy conditional independence or design-known measurement supports.
body.interpretation: The correction is finite-dimensional after conditioning on \(X\), but non-oracle implementation has two distinct regularity demands. Spectral separation makes rank selection benign: fitted eigenvalues above \(\varepsilon/2\) recover the true nonzero eigenspace when the Gram error is small. Structural zeros are different because a fitted probability placed in a latent class--measurement cell that is absent under the truth is not covered by the two-sided conditional-zero score restriction. Its fitted mass therefore appears as an additive, estimable leakage allowance rather than a quadratic product. In a validation design that records the support sets in advance, this allowance is exactly zero; otherwise it must be diagnosed and controlled at the inference rate.
